A cliché ( UK : / ˈ k l iː ʃ eɪ / or US : / k l iː ˈ ʃ eɪ / ; French: [kliʃe] ) is a saying, idea, or element of an artistic work that has become overused to the point of losing its original meaning, novelty, or figurative or artistic power, even to the point of now being bland or uninteresting. [ 1 ] In phraseology , the term has taken on a more technical meaning, referring to an expression imposed by conventionalized linguistic usage . [ 2 ]
